summary: Completed exports use consumer-scoped refs; shared CAS registration and deletion require the same key guard and live-reference authority.
invariants: Reuse preserves the producer and registers a consumer ref after exact committed metadata and bounded streaming SHA/length verification.
Only public-backed journals share CAS keys; local storage keys and export attempt IDs remain unique.
PostgreSQL registration, staging and lifecycle changes acquire the same nonblocking transaction key guard before row locks.
Busy writers roll back and retry; physical deletion requires fresh READ COMMITTED evidence and no live alias or pointer.
GC preserves sibling refcounts and retention windows; SQLite and unsupported snapshot authority defer physical deletion.
Cache-only reuse reports zero worker count/duration; operation duration includes ref verification. Lossy downgrade is rejected.
forbidden: Changing the canonical producer to impersonate a consumer.
Deleting shared bytes while another alias, refcount or pointer remains live.
Replaying tombstoned, deleted or mismatched metadata.
Claiming real PostgreSQL concurrency or production readiness from isolated tests.
